new_defects.title: Workload C applies mutation before initial A index
new_defects.source_evidence: tools/run-systems-workload-v1.py:908-925 applies mutation at lines 909-910 before the initial build at lines 914-920.
impact: does not measure A-to-B incremental maintenance
freshness probe observes pre-indexed B rather than a change made query-visible by incremental processing
C system-under-test clock is a no-change invocation and is not interpretable as incremental update cost
new_defects.minimum_correction: Build incremental.db from unmodified A; apply mutation after initial build; then run incremental_update and compare it with a fresh B full rebuild. Re-run affected C smoke regressions.

M1-M4 bytes/hashes and scope labels exist in all three manifests, but C1 means cross-file invalidation is not exercised after an A baseline.
B2/B3 mutation manifests are present with the V1 family set and frozen hashes.
Nine digest outputs accurately declare six gating fact states and three strict diagnostics, but C1 makes their parity comparison B-versus-B.
Separate update and query-visible freshness fields/probe exist, but C1 means probe success does not establish incremental propagation.
SUT, setup, validation, parity, and end-to-end clocks are separate; C1 invalidates interpretation of C SUT latency, not clock separation.
Each repository has a portable frozen 20-query, four-type manifest and successful smoke anchor validation.
Runner produces promised KLOC/symbol/node/raw-reference normalizations with null for zero denominators.
Expanded provenance and qualification load-note rejection are implemented.
